metadata.title: Computational Skepticism — Trust, But Verify

beats.narration_text: Bonjour — this is Liam, in for Bear. Skepticism sounds like the guy who doubts everything and wears black. It isn't. It's a discipline — and the computational part is how you make it survive the modern firehose of information. Let's take it apart.

props.command: Hey Claude — what is "computational skepticism", and how is it different from just being cynical about everything?
output: Skepticism is evidence — for AND against — not despair.
Act One: what skepticism actually is.

beats.new_visual_element: Act card — Act I: Skepticism Is Not Nihilism

beats.narration_text: The word is old. Greek skeptics like Pyrrho and Sextus Empiricus didn't say nothing is true — they said: suspend the verdict until you've weighed it.
beats.new_visual_element: Ancient skeptic (Pyrrho / Sextus Empiricus) — representative bust/engraving
beats.prompt: PD bust or period engraving of Sextus Empiricus or Pyrrho of Elis (no authentic likeness exists — label as representative). Search: Wikimedia Commons 'Sextus Empiricus', 'Pyrrho'. media/B02.png. Fallback: Remotion type card (re-lane, VOX→~15%).

build.needs: YOU → drop a historical image at media/B02.png (or .mp4)
build.suggested: find: PD bust or period engraving of Sextus Empiricus or Pyrrho of Elis (no authentic likeness exists — label as representative). Search: Wikimedia Commons 'Sextus Empiricus', 'Pyrrho'. media/B02.png. Fallback: Remotion type card (re-lane, VOX→~15%).

beats.narration_text: So skepticism isn't nihilism. Nihilism says nothing matters. Skepticism asks one question, relentlessly: what's the evidence FOR this — and what's the evidence AGAINST?
beats.new_visual_element: Split C2: NIHILISM 'nothing matters' ✗  vs  SKEPTICISM 'what's the evidence?' ✓

production_viz.label: nihilism-vs-skepticism
production_viz.mechanic: Two-column contrast card. Left (muted/ink): NIHILISM — 'nothing matters', a slack down-arrow. Right (terracotta accent): SKEPTICISM — 'what's the evidence FOR? AGAINST?', a balance icon. Right side lands the one terracotta moment.

beats.narration_text: You don't believe or reject. You weigh. If the evidence leans hard one way, you provisionally accept — always ready to re-weigh.
beats.new_visual_element: Balance scale: FOR pan vs AGAINST pan, tipping to a provisional lean

production_viz.label: evidence-scale
production_viz.mechanic: A balance beam. Weights labeled 'for' drop onto the left pan, 'against' onto the right; the beam tips to a PROVISIONAL lean (not slammed to the floor). A 'provisional' tag fades in; a small ↻ re-weigh glyph. EB Garamond labels.

beats.narration_text: And how much evidence you need scales with the stakes. Trivial to be wrong? A little will do. Nuclear-codes wrong? You demand a mountain.
beats.new_visual_element: Curve: evidence threshold rises with stakes (low stakes→little, high stakes→mountain)

production_viz.label: stakes-threshold
production_viz.mechanic: Axes: x = STAKES (low→high), y = EVIDENCE REQUIRED. A rising curve draws on. Two markers ride it: 'trivial' low-left (small dot), 'nuclear codes' high-right (a tall stacked bar / mountain). Terracotta on the high marker.

beats.new_visual_element: Act card — Act II: Why 'Computational'

beats.narration_text: Here's the problem the old skeptics didn't have: the sheer volume. There's more information than any human can weigh — and most of it is competing for your reflex, not your judgment.
beats.new_visual_element: Information firehose — newsstand / feed wall
beats.prompt: Tier 1: a wall of newsprint / a saturated social feed / a newsstand — 'information overload'. AI-generate or stock. media/B07.png.

build.needs: YOU → drop a historical image at media/B07.png (or .mp4)
build.suggested: find: Tier 1: a wall of newsprint / a saturated social feed / a newsstand — 'information overload'. AI-generate or stock. media/B07.png.

beats.narration_text: Worse: it's now trivial to manufacture information that looks real and isn't. The fakes are cheap, fast, and convincing.
beats.new_visual_element: Grid of items, real vs synthetic indistinguishable, flooding in

production_viz.label: real-vs-fake
production_viz.mechanic: A grid of identical-looking cards floods in fast. A few get a small 'real' tick, a few a terracotta 'fake' mark — but they are visually indistinguishable; the marks appear only AFTER, making the point. Volume accelerates.

beats.narration_text: Gathering the complete story by hand — every claim, every counter-claim, every source — might take ten hours. So most people never do it. They skip to belief.
beats.new_visual_element: Stopwatch / '10 hours you won't spend' card

production_viz.label: ten-hours
production_viz.mechanic: A stopwatch winds to 10:00:00 while a stack of 'claim / counter-claim / source' chips piles up; then a hand waves it away and a shortcut arrow jumps straight to 'BELIEF'. Terracotta on the skipped shortcut.

beats.narration_text: That's the computational part. You point algorithms at the question and let them gather the evidence — both sides — so your mind is freed to do the one thing it's for: judge.
beats.new_visual_element: C3 pipeline: query fans out, gathers FOR and AGAINST in parallel, hands to a human

production_viz.label: gather-both-sides
production_viz.mechanic: A single QUESTION node fans out to many workers that return two labeled columns — EVIDENCE FOR / EVIDENCE AGAINST — which flow into a human 'JUDGE' silhouette at the end. The human node is the terracotta moment.

beats.new_visual_element: Act card — Act III: Trust, But Verify

beats.narration_text: Trust, but verify. A Russian proverb Reagan used signing a nuclear treaty in nineteen eighty-seven — because a treaty isn't taken on faith. Neither is a machine's answer.
beats.new_visual_element: Reagan–Gorbachev INF Treaty signing, Dec 1987 (verified)
beats.prompt: Tier 3: Reagan & Gorbachev at the INF Treaty signing, 8 Dec 1987. Many US-gov photos are public domain (Reagan Library / National Archives). Verify the specific photo's rights. media/B12.png. .source.txt sidecar required.

build.needs: YOU → drop a historical image at media/B12.png (or .mp4)
build.suggested: find: Tier 3: Reagan & Gorbachev at the INF Treaty signing, 8 Dec 1987. Many US-gov photos are public domain (Reagan Library / National Archives). Verify the specific photo's rights. media/B12.png. .source.txt sidecar required.

beats.narration_text: So the model does your ten hours in two minutes — it assembles the story, and, crucially, it hands you its sources.
beats.new_visual_element: ASK→RESULT: a prompt returns a sourced brief in seconds

production_viz.label: ask-result-sourced
production_viz.mechanic: A prompt line resolves into a compact brief whose lines each sprout a numbered [source] chip. Emphasize the source chips appearing — that's the payload. Terracotta on the [sources] row.

beats.narration_text: First verification move: ask a different model the same thing. Where they agree, your confidence rises. Where they split, you've found exactly what to dig into.
beats.new_visual_element: N models queried; agreement vs disagreement tally

production_viz.label: cross-check
production_viz.mechanic: Three model nodes answer the same claim. Two align (✓ ✓) and a confidence bar rises; the third diverges (✗) and gets a terracotta ring labeled 'dig here'. The disagreement is highlighted as the signal, not the noise.

beats.narration_text: Second move, the non-negotiable one: go to the sources it cited. The model is a starting point, not an authority. It can be confidently wrong — verifying is the whole job.
beats.new_visual_element: C3: arrow from the answer to the PRIMARY SOURCE; a 'the tool can be wrong' stamp

production_viz.label: go-to-source
production_viz.mechanic: The model's answer card connects by a bold arrow to an actual SOURCE document. A rubber-stamp 'CAN BE WRONG' lands on the answer card (terracotta); the source doc gets the check. Message: authority lives in the source, not the summary.

beats.narration_text: Take a claim you might meet: a public figure who once called a rival unfit now praises them. The skeptic doesn't believe or dismiss — you ask what's the evidence, what's the counter, what do the primary sources say, and is there any principled reason for the flip.
beats.new_visual_element: Abstracted worked example (UN-NAMED): test a 'reversed stance' claim via the method

production_viz.label: worked-example-abstract
production_viz.mechanic: Two neutral silhouette cards: 'THEN: called unfit' → 'NOW: praises'. Below, four method chips light up in sequence: EVIDENCE FOR · EVIDENCE AGAINST · PRIMARY SOURCE · PRINCIPLED REASON? — the last with a terracotta question mark. NO names, NO real people, NO asserted claim; the beat is the METHOD.

beats.new_visual_element: Act card — Act IV: The Human Decides

beats.narration_text: The tools give you the complete story — not the convenient slice. But they don't decide. A human being reads it and says: this I believe, this I don't.
beats.new_visual_element: A person at a desk, weighing / deciding
beats.prompt: Tier 1: a person at a desk reading/weighing documents, deciding — contemplative, not stock-cheesy. AI-generate or stock. media/B18.png.

build.needs: YOU → drop a historical image at media/B18.png (or .mp4)
build.suggested: find: Tier 1: a person at a desk reading/weighing documents, deciding — contemplative, not stock-cheesy. AI-generate or stock. media/B18.png.

beats.narration_text: And it scales. If you care about something, you don't run one search — you set agents watching it around the clock. That's later in the course.
beats.new_visual_element: Always-on agents monitoring a topic 24/7

production_viz.label: always-on-agents
production_viz.mechanic: A central TOPIC node ringed by small agent nodes that pulse in rotation around a clock face (24/7). New evidence chips ping in over time. One agent pulses terracotta as it flags something.

beats.narration_text: That's what computational skepticism is for: not doubt for its own sake, but tools that let a human hold the complete story — and fight misinformation with evidence.
beats.new_visual_element: Mission card: tools + evidence vs misinformation

production_viz.label: mission
production_viz.mechanic: A clean statement card: 'TOOLS + EVIDENCE → the complete story'. A faint 'misinformation' noise field behind it recedes as the evidence stack builds in front. Terracotta on 'evidence'.

beats.narration_text: Thanks Bear, let's recap with Claude. Skepticism is evidence for AND against, not nihilism. Scale the evidence to the stakes. Automate the gathering. Cross-check the models. Go to the sources. And then — a human renders the verdict.
beats.new_visual_element: Verdict recap card (six moves)

artifactLines: Evidence FOR and AGAINST — not nihilism
Scale the evidence to the stakes

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: pick one claim you care about. Ask for the strongest evidence for it and the strongest against it — then open its top two sources yourself and confirm they say what it claims. Notice how often the source is weaker than the summary. Liam, in for Bear.

beats.narration_text: Computational skepticism. Trust — but verify.
